mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission-enforcement fact lets a Customer-role caller succeed at an operation (ClaimApp) that the matrix forbids. Both LeastPrivilege (matrix check) and FR_002_CustomerLimited (per-role surface) should catch this.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.succeeded = BTrue and op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = ClaimApp }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing audit-completeness lets the model invent a state where an application reached UnderReview without its Submitted->UnderReview audit entry. The pattern and the FR are both supposed to catch a missing entry.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some a: LoanApplication | a.status = UnderReview and (no e: AuditEntry | e.app = a and e.newStatus = UnderReview) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the no-duplicates fact permits two distinct audit entries for the same (app, transition), which structurally corresponds to a re-write of an existing entry — the append-only invariant the FR-018 / FR-022 assertions must catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.app = e2.app and e1.newStatus = e2.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the partial-unique-index constraint lets a single customer hold two simultaneous Submitted/UnderReview applications, which is exactly what FR-008 forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OneInFlightViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = a2.customer and a1.status in (Submitted + UnderReview) and a2.status in (Submitted + UnderReview) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this constraint lets an unrelated loan officer successfully decide an application not assigned to them — the exact failure mode FR-013 names.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnlyAssignedDecidesViolation { some op: Operation | op.succeeded = BTrue and op.kind = DecideApp and op.caller != op.target.assignedOfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing actor-attribution lets the model record an initial-submission audit entry whose actor is a loan officer rather than the application's customer, which AttributionCorrectness is meant to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some e: AuditEntry | (no e.prevStatus) and e.actor.role = LoanOfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the ownership check lets a customer successfully GET an application that does not belong to them, which both OwnershipBasedAccess and FR_020 must reject.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some op: Operation | op.succeeded = BTrue and op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = GetApp and op.target.customer != op.caller }
